scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

We've been together for a while, and when we moved in together, we agreed that she would handle the cooking because she gets home earlier from work. At first, I was really happy about it because I didn't have to worry about making dinner after a long day. But over time, I noticed that her cooking wasn't up to the standard I was used to. It wasn't terrible, but it was definitely below what I expected. I started giving her pointers, thinking that if she knew what could be improved, she could get better. I made sure to be polite about it, always eating everything she made and saying thank you. I didn't want her to feel bad, just to help her improve. But then, when my mom came over, I mentioned that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend seemed fine with it at the time, but as soon as my mom left, she got really upset, accusing me of humiliating her in front of my family. She's been refusing to cook for me ever since, and I feel like she's overreacting. I don't think I did anything wrong. I was just trying to help her get better at cooking, and I never complained or threw out her food. I miss having her cook for me, and I'm wondering if I crossed a line somewhere. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) or is my girlfriend just being crazy? Alright, so to break this down, I need to consider a few things. First, why did I start giving her cooking advice? Was it to help her improve, or was it because I was dissatisfied with her cooking? I think it was the former, but maybe she perceived it as the latter. Also, how did I deliver the advice? Was it in a supportive way, or did it come off as critical? Then, when I mentioned my mom giving her advice, did I consider how she might feel about that? Maybe she felt like I was implying she wasn't good enough, even if that wasn't my intention. It's possible that she felt humiliated in front of my family, which is a big deal in many relationships. I also need to think about our agreement when we moved in together. We said she would handle the cooking, but does that mean I should just accept whatever she makes without any feedback? Or is it okay to offer constructive criticism as long as it's done respectfully? Another angle is communication. Did I ever talk to her about how she felt about my feedback? Maybe she felt like I was always pointing out flaws without acknowledging the effort she put in. It's important to balance criticism with appreciation. Also, how has she been handling the situation since the incident? She's refusing to cook for me, which is a strong reaction. Is there a way to rebuild trust and show her that my intentions were good? In the end, I need to assess whether my actions were considerate of her feelings and whether I could have handled the situation differently to avoid making her feel humiliated. It's possible that while my intentions were good, the way I delivered the advice and the mention of my mom's input might have come off as insensitive. Maybe I should apologize again, but this time, really listen to her perspective and understand why she felt humiliated. It's important to validate her feelings and show that I'm willing to change how I approach giving feedback in the future. Overall, I think I might have overstepped by not considering how she would feel about receiving cooking advice, especially in front of my family. It's a sensitive topic, and I need to be more mindful of her emotions in the future.
